items.title: 18.8 Stability of Complexes and Stability Constant (Kstab)

source_refs.note: Topic 18.8 with Table 18.5 and Quick Check 18.6, answered (PDF 30-31). The book's [Cu(NH3)6]2- and its 6NH3 equation are corrected to [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+; the chelate equation is given with charges. Answers need review.

blocks.text: The stability constant, Kstab, is the equilibrium constant for the formation of a complex ion from its constituent ions or molecules in a solvent. In water, water is the first ligand; a new ligand competes with it for the metal ion. For example:

The concentration of water, the solvent, stays effectively constant and is left out of the Kstab expression. Stability constants are usually given as log10 Kstab, which makes very large numbers easy to compare. The higher log10 Kstab, the more stable the complex and the further the equilibrium lies to the right; the lower it is, the less stable the complex and the more easily its ligands are displaced.

blocks.caption: Stability constants of some copper(II) complexes (book's Table 18.5)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Table 18.5 prints the ammonia complex as [Cu(NH3)6]2-. The copper(II) ammonia complex with log10 Kstab = 13.1 is [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ (often written [Cu(NH3)4]2+), a positive ion.

Complexes of polydentate ligands have higher stability constants than those of monodentate ligands; this is the chelate effect, e.g. [Cu(H2O)6]2+ + 3en -> [Cu(en)3]2+ + 6H2O. A ligand that gives a higher Kstab can displace one that gives a lower Kstab: adding ammonia to the yellow chloride complex turns the solution deep blue, because the ammonia complex is much more stable: [CuCl4]2- + 6NH3 -> [Cu(NH3)6]2+ + 4Cl-. Conversely, diluting a complex with a large amount of water can push the equilibrium back to the left, re-forming the hydrated ion.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Ammonia replaces only four ligands of copper(II): [CuCl4]2- + 4NH3 + 2H2O -> [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ + 4Cl-.

items: Write the Kstab expression for the formation of [Cu(NH3)4]2+ from [Cu(H2O)6]2+ and NH3.
Using log10 Kstab for [CuCl4]2- (5.6) and [Cu(EDTA)]2- (18.8), explain why polydentate ligands form more stable complexes.
Write the equation for the first step of the stepwise replacement of water by ammonia in [Cu(H2O)6]2+.
